title: Strict structures and intertwining arrows under a natural comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category [def-nagata-category], let $F,G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ be endofunctors, and let $\kappa:F\xrightarrow{\sim}G$ be a natural isomorphism. Thus, for each $h:M\to N$, $G(h)\circ\kappa_M=\kappa_N\circ F(h)$. Give $M,N\in\mathcal C$ morphisms $\varphi_M:G(M)\to M$ and $\varphi_N:G(N)\to N$, and set $u_M=\varphi_M\circ\kappa_M$ and $u_N=\varphi_N\circ\kappa_N$. Then
$$h\circ\varphi_M=\varphi_N\circ G(h)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h\circ u_M=u_N\circ F(h).$$
The lower arrow in both squares is the same $h$; the upper arrows are $G(h)$ and $F(h)$ respectively. If $\varphi_M$ is invertible, then $u_M$ is invertible with
$$u_M^{-1}=\kappa_M^{-1}\circ\varphi_M^{-1},\qquad u_M^{-1}\circ u_M=\mathrm{id}_{F(M)},\qquad u_M\circ u_M^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_M.$$
The same assertion holds for $N$. Consequently these formulas send strict $G$-fixed pairs and their intertwining arrows to strict $F$-fixed pairs and their intertwining arrows [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], without changing any underlying object or arrow.

source.place: Entire proof: comparison of the two pullbacks, compatibility with pullback-composition and f, and preservation of the squares

proof.text:
For the forward implication, assume $h\circ\varphi_M=\varphi_N\circ G(h)$. Substitution of $u_M,u_N$, associativity [def-nagata-category], and the stated naturality equation give
$$h\circ u_M=(h\circ\varphi_M)\circ\kappa_M=\varphi_N\circ G(h)\circ\kappa_M=\varphi_N\circ\kappa_N\circ F(h)=u_N\circ F(h).$$
Both sides are maps $F(M)\to N$; only the upper arrow has changed from $G(h)$ to $F(h)$, while the lower arrow is $h$.

source.place: Entire proof: comparison of the two pullbacks, compatibility with pullback-composition and f, and preservation of the squares

proof.text:
Conversely assume $h\circ u_M=u_N\circ F(h)$. Substituting the definitions and the stated naturality equation yields
$$(h\circ\varphi_M)\circ\kappa_M=(\varphi_N\circ G(h))\circ\kappa_M.$$
Precompose both sides with $\kappa_M^{-1}:G(M)\to F(M)$. Associativity and $\kappa_M\circ\kappa_M^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{G(M)}$ reduce this equality to $h\circ\varphi_M=\varphi_N\circ G(h)$. This is an explicit cancellation using the inverse given by the natural isomorphism, not an assumption on $h$ or on either $\varphi$.

source.place: Entire proof: comparison of the two pullbacks, compatibility with pullback-composition and f, and preservation of the squares

proof.text:
If $\varphi_M$ is invertible, put $v_M=\kappa_M^{-1}\circ\varphi_M^{-1}:M\to F(M)$. Associativity and the defining inverse equations give
$$v_M\circ u_M=\kappa_M^{-1}\circ(\varphi_M^{-1}\circ\varphi_M)\circ\kappa_M=\kappa_M^{-1}\circ\kappa_M=\mathrm{id}_{F(M)},$$
$$u_M\circ v_M=\varphi_M\circ(\kappa_M\circ\kappa_M^{-1})\circ\varphi_M^{-1}=\varphi_M\circ\varphi_M^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_M.$$
Thus $v_M=u_M^{-1}$. Replacing $M$ by $N$ in these same two equations proves the assertion for $N$ whenever $\varphi_N$ is invertible.

source.place: Entire proof: comparison of the two pullbacks, compatibility with pullback-composition and f, and preservation of the squares

proof.text: By [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], a strict $G$-fixed pair is precisely $(M,\varphi_M)$ with invertible structure map, and an arrow between two such pairs is an underlying $h$ satisfying the left-hand intertwiner equation. Step 3 gives a strict $F$-fixed pair $(M,u_M)$; steps 1 and 2 identify exactly the allowed underlying arrows. Assign $(M,\varphi_M)\mapsto(M,u_M)$ and $h\mapsto h$. Identities and composites in each fixed-pair category are those in $\mathcal C$, so this assignment preserves them literally. The objects of $\mathcal C$ and the underlying arrows are unchanged.

lean.statement: theorem naturalComparisonStrictIntertwiners {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (F G : C ⥤ C) (kappa : F ≅ G) (M N : C) (phiM : G.obj M ⟶ M) (phiN : G.obj N ⟶ N) (h : M ⟶ N) : ((phiM ≫ h = G.map h ≫ phiN) ↔ ((kappa.hom.app M ≫ phiM) ≫ h = F.map h ≫ (kappa.hom.app N ≫ phiN))) ∧ (∀ (_hM : IsIso phiM), IsIso (kappa.hom.app M ≫ phiM) ∧ inv (kappa.hom.app M ≫ phiM) = inv phiM ≫ kappa.inv.app M ∧ (kappa.hom.app M ≫ phiM) ≫ (inv phiM ≫ kappa.inv.app M) = 𝟙 (F.obj M) ∧ (inv phiM ≫ kappa.inv.app M) ≫ (kappa.hom.app M ≫ phiM) = 𝟙 M) ∧ (∀ (_hN : IsIso phiN), IsIso (kappa.hom.app N ≫ phiN) ∧ inv (kappa.hom.app N ≫ phiN) = inv phiN ≫ kappa.inv.app N ∧ (kappa.hom.app N ≫ phiN) ≫ (inv phiN ≫ kappa.inv.app N) = 𝟙 (F.obj N) ∧ (inv phiN ≫ kappa.inv.app N) ≫ (kappa.hom.app N ≫ phiN) = 𝟙 N) ∧ (∃ T : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun A : Algebra G ↦ IsIso A.str) ⥤ ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun A : Algebra F ↦ IsIso A.str), T ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι (fun A : Algebra F ↦ IsIso A.str) = ObjectProperty.ι (fun A : Algebra G ↦ IsIso A.str) ⋙ functorOfNatTrans kappa.hom)
